note: ⛔ SNG-623 — CCODE: '`rules.martial` is completely empty. Every band dial in the game is a code default today. They all work, and NONE OF THEM IS A DECISION ANYBODY MADE. If you want the band layer to be yours, that file is where it becomes yours.' ⛑ SO IT IS AUTHORED. Each number below was the engine's fallback and is now a ruling with a reason — where I have kept the default, that is a CHOICE and the reason says so.
_bandAtSlots: ⛑ KEPT AT 3. Three company slots is the point where you stop travelling with people and start leading them — two is a pair and four is already an organisation. ⚠️ It is also the first rung where a loss is felt as a gap rather than as a death.
_bandAtHoldings: ⛑ KEPT AT 2. One holding is a home; two is a thing that needs somebody in it while you are elsewhere, which is the whole reason a band exists.
_lossPerTide: ⛑ KEPT AT 0.12. Roughly one in eight per tide is the rate at which a unit BLEEDS rather than breaks — high enough that a long campaign costs people, low enough that a single bad tide is not a wipe. ⚠️ It compounds with `unwardedLossMult`, so an unshielded band actually runs at ~17%.
_reachWeight: ⛔ SNG-659 §1 (Erik): "if those few have good skills that hit multiple people, we need to account for that… it SHOULD matter who the defenders are." A named figure with a craft reaching N counts as `quality × (1 + (N−1) × this)`. ⚠️ BOTH LITERAL READINGS FAIL, measured against §1d over 3,000 clashes: at 0 (herself plus N−1 soldiers) the lone epic holds 0% against a target of two-in-three, and at 1 (N of her) every row is 100% — the "one wizard beats an army" failure §1c.4 exists to prevent. 0.4 fits the four numbered targets best (total error 0.69, against 1.59 at 0.2 and 0.93 at 0.5). ⬜ AND IT IS A DIAL BECAUSE TWO OF THE TARGETS CANNOT BOTH BE MET: row 2 is three heroics and row 3 is one epic, wanted at 70% and 67%, and under any rule where quality AND reach both count, three heroics beat one epic. Row 2 overshoots at every k that gets row 3 right.
_reachExchanges: ⛔ §1c.4 — "a clash lasts exchanges, not one swing… a caster who empties early fades." Energy pays for `floor(energy / energyCost)` of these exchanges at wide reach and the rest at single reach, and the figure's weight is the average. Measured: an epic with energy for THREE uses holds 61%; the same epic with energy for ONE holds 0%. This is the limit that stops a many-target craft being a superpower.
_areaToFigures: ⛑ §1c.5 — how many figures a ZONE holds, since `area` is a zone and not a count. Aevi proposed 2. Exactly one craft in the corpus carries BOTH fields and so states the ratio itself — `keening`, `area: 5` and `targets: 6` — which is 1.2. One authored pair is weak evidence, and 2 has none. ⬜ AND §1c.5's PROSE CLAUSE HAS NO POPULATION: all 14 authored areas are numeric, so nothing was built for it.
_guardAbsorbShare: ⛔ §1c.2 — "the FIRST losses on the guarded side are absorbed." The guard absorbs up to its own quality, but never more than this share of what the line would have lost. ⚠️ UNCAPPED IT IS NOT A FLOOR, IT IS IMMUNITY: measured, a heroic guard took a six-strong line from 1.80 average losses to 0.00 — a guard winning a fight it is meant to SURVIVE. At a half it takes 1.80 to 1.00 at six strong and 3.26 to 2.00 at forty: fewer at every scale, never none, which is what "holds noticeably longer" should mean.
_unwardedLossMult: ⛑ KEPT AT 1.4. Nothing shields them, so the same tide takes more of them — and 1.4 is the size of the gap that makes warding worth paying for without making an unwarded band unplayable.
_condition: ⛑ THE THREE RUNGS, KEPT: blooded at any loss (×0.9), WORN past a quarter gone (×0.7), BROKEN past half (×0.3). ⚠️ THE SHAPE IS THE RULING RATHER THAN THE NUMBERS: the fall from worn to broken is more than twice the fall from blooded to worn, because **a unit that has lost half of itself does not fight at half strength — it fights like a unit that is about to run.** A linear ladder would say the opposite and would be wrong about people.
_bandThreatScale: ⛑ KEPT AT 6, against `sqrt(effective)` — so a band's threat grows with the ROOT of its size. ⚠️ Doubling a unit does not double what it can do to you, which is the same reason a mob is not an army.
_leaderStep: ⛔ ERIK RULED THE LADDER AND CCODE USED MINE — `1 + floor(level/10)` without the base, capped so a leader can at most DOUBLE his unit. ⛑ Ten is the right step because it is the same interval the rest of the game already moves on, and the cap is the real ruling: **a commander is a multiplier on people who exist, never a substitute for them.**
_callCostPerHead: ⛔ THE NUMBER CCODE ASKED FOR, AND IT IS NOT THE WAGE. He fell back to `wagePerHand` (3) and said so on the screen — *'no martial rule sets this yet; a called head is paid what a working hand is paid.'* ⚠️ **CALLING SOMEBODY TO FIGHT SHOULD COST MORE THAN ASKING THEM TO WORK.** Four rather than three: a third again, which is small enough that a small call is affordable and large enough that a standing legion is a decision you make on purpose. ⛑ And it keeps the two numbers visibly different, so nobody reads the fallback as the rule.
_whatIsStillNotMine: ⬜ THE COMMANDER CRAFTS. `leaderBonusOf` carries no parameter yet, deliberately — CCode: 'a parameter nothing fills reads to the next author as a built system.' ⚠️ `the_gathering`, `raise_banner`, `lead_the_line` and `command_field` are what reach PAST the doubling ceiling, which is what makes them worth authoring rather than decorative. **That is the next thing I owe this file.**
_trainedCallMult: ⛔ CCODE-430 LEFT THIS UNAUTHORED AND STOOD 0.75 IN, SAYING SO ON SCREEN. Authored at exactly that, and not because it was the fallback — because of what it MEANS. ⛑  is 4 and  is 3, and I set that gap myself: calling somebody to fight costs more than asking them to work. ⚠️ **A YARD CLOSES THE GAP EXACTLY.** 4 × 0.75 = 3, so a hold with a muster yard calls a head for what it pays a working hand — because at a yard the training is already done, and what you are paying for is the person rather than the readiness. ⛔ THE NUMBER IS THE SENTENCE: a yard does not make war cheap, it makes it cost what work costs. ⬜ And it is the only multiplier I would put here; a second training tier would buy a discount on a discount, which is where a dial stops meaning anything.
